section: Tekton Results concepts
job_statement: When I need to understand how pipeline runs and task runs are archived, I want to learn about results and records concepts, so I can effectively use Tekton Results for observability.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
related_jobs: Search for results using CEL queries
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to understand Tekton Results architecture
Ensure clarity on result and record naming conventions
Reduce likelihood of confusion between results and records
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Tekton Results concepts, lines 73-245
notes: Conceptual understanding of Tekton Results data model. Explains results contain records, naming format, and YAML manifest preservation.

section: Configuring LokiStack forwarding for logging information
job_statement: When I need to access logging information for task runs, I want to configure forwarding to LokiStack, so I can query logs after pipeline runs and task runs are deleted.
parent_job: Configure Tekton Results for production use
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to enable log forwarding
Ensure log information is preserved after resource deletion
Reduce likelihood of configuration errors
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Configuring LokiStack forwarding for logging information, lines 273-395
notes: Requires LokiStack and OpenShift Logging installation. Configuration differs between OpenShift Logging v5 and v6.

section: Configuring an external database server
job_statement: When I need production-grade data storage for Tekton Results, I want to configure an external PostgreSQL database, so I can ensure data durability and performance for business-critical workloads.
parent_job: Configure Tekton Results for production use
prerequisites: Have access to PostgreSQL-compatible database server
desired_outcomes: Minimize reliance on default internal database
Ensure automated backups are available
Reduce likelihood of data loss in production
Enable performance tuning capabilities
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Configuring an external database server, lines 404-451
notes: Default internal PostgreSQL instance not suitable for production. External database provides automated backups, performance tuning, storage lifecycle management.

section: Configuring the retention policy for Tekton Results
job_statement: When I need to manage storage resources efficiently, I want to configure a retention policy for Tekton Results, so I can remove older results and prevent unnecessary storage use and database performance degradation.
parent_job: Configure Tekton Results for production use
desired_outcomes: Minimize storage resource consumption
Reduce likelihood of database performance degradation
Ensure data is retained for required compliance period
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Configuring the retention policy for Tekton Results, lines 461-497
notes: Default retention is indefinite. Allows cron-based scheduling and configurable retention period in days.

section: Observability metrics for Tekton Results
job_statement: When I need to monitor Tekton Results performance, I want to view metrics for storage and deletion operations, so I can identify performance issues and runs deleted before successful storage.
parent_job: Monitor Tekton Results health and performance
prerequisites: Configure ServiceMonitor resources for Tekton Results
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to identify storage latency issues
Reduce likelihood of undetected storage failures
Ensure visibility into deletion performance
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Observability metrics for Tekton Results, lines 506-600
notes: Metrics exposed on port 9090 at /metrics endpoint. Includes storage performance, storage failures, deletion duration, and deletion count metrics with labels for filtering.

section: Preparing the opc utility environment for querying Tekton Results
job_statement: When I need to query Tekton Results from the command line, I want to prepare the opc utility environment, so I can authenticate and access the Tekton Results API.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to set up authentication
Reduce likelihood of authentication errors
Ensure persistent authentication configuration
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Preparing the opc utility environment for querying Tekton Results, lines 628-680
notes: Requires setting RESULTS_API environment variable, creating authentication token, and optionally creating ~/.config/tkn/results.yaml for automatic authentication.

section: Querying for results and records by name
job_statement: When I need to retrieve specific pipeline run or task run information, I want to query results and records by name, so I can view YAML manifests and logs after the original resources are deleted.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to locate specific run information
Ensure access to complete YAML manifests
Reduce dependency on active pipeline runs and task runs
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Querying for results and records by name, lines 689-783
notes: Allows listing all results in namespace, listing records in result, retrieving YAML manifests, and retrieving logs using record names.

section: Searching for results
job_statement: When I need to find pipeline runs and task runs by specific criteria, I want to search for results using CEL queries, so I can identify failed runs or runs with specific annotations.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to find runs matching specific criteria
Reduce manual filtering effort
Ensure accurate identification of failed or annotated runs
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Searching for results, lines 792-824
notes: Uses CEL queries to filter results. Examples include finding failed runs and finding runs with specific annotations. Most relevant information is in record objects.

section: Searching for records
job_statement: When I need to find specific pipeline runs or task runs by detailed criteria, I want to search for records using CEL queries, so I can filter by names, completion times, pipeline associations, and other YAML data.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to find runs by complex criteria
Ensure access to full YAML data for filtering
Reduce manual inspection of multiple runs
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Searching for records, lines 833-901
notes: Records contain full YAML manifests allowing rich filtering. Examples include finding failed runs, runs by name, task runs for specific pipeline run, runs associated with specific pipeline, runs by duration, completion date, task count, and annotations.

section: Reference information for searching results
job_statement: When I need to construct CEL queries for results, I want to understand available fields and values, so I can create accurate search expressions.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to learn query syntax
Reduce likelihood of query errors
Ensure correct field usage
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Reference information for searching results, lines 910-953
notes: Reference material for CEL query fields including parent, uid, annotations, summary, create_time, update_time, and summary.status values.

section: Reference information for searching records
job_statement: When I need to construct CEL queries for records, I want to understand available fields and data structure, so I can create complex searches using YAML manifest data.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to learn record query syntax
Ensure correct access to YAML data elements
Reduce likelihood of query errors
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Reference information for searching records, lines 962-989
notes: Reference material for CEL query fields including name, data_type, and data (entire YAML manifest). Data field allows querying any YAML element.

section: Viewing result information for a pipeline run
job_statement: When I need detailed information about a completed pipeline run, I want to view its description, manifest, and logs, so I can troubleshoot issues or verify execution details.
parent_job: Access archived pipeline and task run information
prerequisites: Have pipeline run name or UUID
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to retrieve pipeline run details
Ensure access to complete execution information
Reduce need to inspect multiple resources
evidence: using-tekton-results-for-openshift-pipelines-observability.adoc -> Viewing result information for a pipeline run, lines 1231-1328
notes: Can describe pipeline run showing status, params, workspaces, and task runs. Can output full YAML manifest. Pipeline run logs exclude task run logs which must be queried separately.

notes: Can describe task run showing status and params. Can output full YAML manifest. Requires LokiStack configuration to retrieve logs.
